## Why this course?

## Primary means of communication

\- Speech is the primary means of communication for almost every social group

## Most widespread means of communication

## Most widespread means of communication

\- Speech is the most human characteristic: Understanding the integration of language (i.a. phonology) and the mechanics of speech (i.e. phonetics) is key to understanding what makes our species unique

## What is phonetics?

## Definitions

\- Study of the physical reality of the speech sounds

\- Phonetics is concerned with describing the speech sounds that occur in the languages of the world (Ladefoged, 1993)

\- The study of speech sounds. It is a wide-ranging field, and it does not necessarily have a direct connection with the study of language itself. It deals with the physical reality of speech sounds (Kelly, 2000)

\- The study of the physiological, aerodynamic, and acoustic characteristics of speech-sounds (Catford, 2001)

## What is phonology?

## Definitions

\- Study of the functional/linguistic reality of the speech sounds

\- Phonology is the description of the systems and patterns of sounds that occur in a language (Ladefoged, 2006)

\- The study of the abstract side of the sounds of language (Roach, 2000)

## Basic unit: the phoneme

-   Phonemes: Sounds that make it possible to distinguish two words with different meanings
-   Language-specific discrete segments
-   Minimal pairs: Make it possible to establish the phonological inventory of a language (e.g., /pɑt/ vs /kɑt/)

| -120 | -80 | -60 | -40 | -20 |  0  | 20  | 40  | 60  | 80  | 120 |
|:----:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|

What you heard vs. What you perceived.

But in Thai...

## Phonemes and phonetic variation (Continued)

VOT (DEV) phonétique vs voisement phonologique

What you heard:

-   In Dutch: `/b/` vs `/p/`
-   In Thai: `/b/` vs `/p/` vs `/pʰ/`
-   In English (in initial position): `/b/` vs `/p/`

## Phonemes and phonetic variation (Allophones)

-   Allophones (Free distribution): Sounds that do not convey a difference in meaning between two morphemes
-   E.g., in French `[puʀ]` « for » vs `[pur]` « for » vs `[puʁ]` « for »
    -   Voiced uvular fricative `[ʁ]`
    -   Voiceless uvular fricative `[χ]`
    -   Alveolar trill `[r]`
-   But in some Dutch dialects: `[r]` et `[χ]` are different realizations of the phonemes `/r/` and `/χ/` (`/rudə/` roede vs `/χudə/` goeden)

## Phonemes and phonetic variation (Contextual)

::: {layout-ncol="2"}
<!-- ![](./Media/LTVQ/image41.png "Context 1") -->

<!-- ![](./Media/LTVQ/image42.png "Context 2") -->
:::

-   Allophones (contextual distribution): In the English words *tea*, *steam* and *sit*
-   Perception of the « same » consonant `/t/` $\rightarrow$ `[tʰi:]` $\neq$ `[sti:m]` $\neq$ `[sɪt̚]` (aspirated vs unreleased)
-   But in Thai: `[tʰ]` and `[t]` represent distinct phonemic contrasts (`/tun/` realization vs `/tʰun/` accumulate)

## Summary Matrix

| Relationship Type       | Influence of Context? | Same Meaning? | Result                            |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| 2 speech sounds         | No                    | No            | 2 Phonemes                        |
| Free distribution       | No                    | Yes           | 1 Phoneme (Free Allophones)       |
| Contextual distribution | Yes                   | Yes           | 1 Phoneme (Contextual Allophones) |

## The IPA 😇 What?

-   International Phonetic Alphabet $\rightarrow$ standardized transcription system

-   +/- 100 symbols, 50 diacritic marks

-   A separate symbol indicates an attested phonemic contrast in one or more languages

<!-- ![](./Media/LTVQ/image43.png "IPA Chart Overview") -->

## The IPA 😇 What for?

-   Representation of the speech signal according to clear conventions

-   Choices must be made (e.g., Belgian French *il tombe encore*) \* From broad - phonemic: `/il tɔ̃b ɑ̃kɔʁ/` \* To narrow - phonetic: `[il tɔ̃ːp ɑ̃kɔʀ̥]`

## The IPA 😇 Knowledge & Training

-   Partially covered in class, but self-training is key!

-   Resources: *Seeing Speech*, *Official IPA*, *Berkeley Online*

## The IPA 😇 Tips and tricks

-   Contrastive listening

-   Self-production and exploration of speech organs (using a mirror, placing a hand to feel airflow, inhaling to identify articulation paths)

-   Recording and listening to your own production

## Scottish English Conclusion

\- This is a **contrastive distribution** (phonemic difference).

## Phonological Distribution

Describe the distribution of `[x]` and `[g]` based on the following corpus:

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Forms with `[x]`

-   `[alax-aa]` *to undo*
-   `[hawex-aa]` *to cover*
-   `[lapax-aa]` *to hit*
-   `[lawax-aa]` *to block*
-   `[nenex-aa]` *to follow*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Forms with `[g]`

-   `[alag-ia]` *undo it*
-   `[haweg-ia]` *cover it*
-   `[lapag-ia]` *hit it*
-   `[lawag-ia]` *block it*
-   `[neneg-ia]` *follow it*
:::
:::

## Wuvulu Analysis & Conclusion

\- 2 allophones in **contextual variation**: \* `[x]` appears before the suffix `-aa` \* `[g]` appears before the suffix `-ia`

**Is phonetics part of linguistics?**

## Phonetics vs. Phonology Hierarchy

-   **Phonetics:** The physical realization of speech production and perception.
-   **Phonology:** Study of the conveyed linguistic meaning.

## Structural Viewpoint

Strictly speaking, pure phonetics is often classified as "outside" abstract linguistics, acting instead as the physical vehicle for phonological systems.

## Laboratory Phonology

\- First conference (LabPhon) in 1987.

\- Awareness that phonological knowledge is better described through continuous phonetic events rather than rigid, isolated categorical blocks.

\- Legacy of J.J. Ohala (1941-2020).

<!-- ![](./Media/LTVQ/image52.png "LabPhon Intersection diagram") -->

## Recording Protocol in Praat

-   Launch Praat. Connect an external microphone.
-   Select: **New \> Record mono Sound**.

<!-- ![](./Media/LTVQ/image77.png "Praat Interface Record Menu") -->

## Audio Quality Optimization

-   **Sampling Rate:** Keep default at 44,100 Hz.
-   Run laptop on battery power to isolate electrical cycle hums.
-   Record in a quiet room to maintain a stable baseline noise floor.

<!-- ![](./Media/LTVQ/image80.png "Audio level calibration capture") -->
